mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as observed in historical data.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 9.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in residential sales (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) indicates broad economic weakness that depresses consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS and PAYEMS both decline, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), increased borrowing costs and reduced liquidity cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as evidenced by historical policy shifts.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles, or Rank IC for regime falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 95, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) below 600 thousand units signals weak residential construction that reduces consumer spending and economic momentum, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is below 600, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and unemployment (UNRATE) signals stagflation that erodes corporate profit margins and consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 9.0%), reduced consumer spending and corporate revenue growth cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as observed during labor market crises.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.0%, or Rank IC for regime falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
